newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs higher, rate fears fade on Tokai Kogyo reports.
newsitem.headline: JGBs higher, rate fears fade on Tokai Kogyo reports.

text.p: Key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures rose sharply in early afternoon trade on Friday in reaction to media reports that construction firm Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd is preparing to apply for court protection from creditors under Japanese law.

The reports eased traders' concerns that the Bank of Japan will raise interest rates in the near future as bad loan problems among general construction and real estate companies are still hampering a recovery in the economy, traders said.
The September stood at 125.17 at 0435 GMT, up 0.44 from Thursday. It rose as high as 125.24 after the reports.
"That was a buy," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit. "We had not forgotten about problems at construction companies. But at last, the problems have come to light."

Tokai Kogyo shares were suspended from trade on the Tokyo bourse on Friday afternoon after Jiji new agency, quoting unnamed sources, reported that the company had debts totalling 520 billion yen and has sought for the court protection.

Tokai Kogyo later told Reuters that its board had begun meeting at 1.00 p.m. (0400 GMT) to discuss ways of restructuring, including applying for court protection under the Japanese bankruptcy laws due to its financial difficulties.
The yield of key 182nd 10-year JGB fell as low as 2.250 percent. It finished at 2.295 percent on Thursday.
